paras.en: Or, [[3:17|The labour of the olive tree shall fail|Mentietur opus olivæ]]: because many are willing to have pity on others and to help them, and do not have pity on their own souls nor come to their aid, though they never cease to wound them daily with vices, and neither repent nor amend. Therefore it is said in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 30:24|Have pity on thy own soul, pleasing God|Miserere animæ tuæ placens Deo]]. And Christ in Matthew: [[Matt 16:26|what doth it profit a man, if he gain the whole world and suffer the loss of his own soul?|Quid prodest homini, si universum mundum lucretur, animæ vero suæ detrimentum patiatur?]] Let charity and piety, then, begin with themselves, and so be passed on to others.

paras.t: Denique, sicut in Prophetis per ficum, vineam, et olivam designatur multoties Synagoga, ita in novo Testamento per eadem significatur Ecclesia. Unde et ista de Synagoga possunt intelligi : quæ præsertim post Christi adventum cessavit florere ac fructificare, cœpitque tunc contra Christum mentiri, blasphemare, et fallere. Nam et per ficum, cui Christus ante maledixit, ita quod aruit, figurabatur tunc Synagoga infertilis.
paras.en: Lastly, as in the Prophets the Synagogue is many times signified by the fig tree, the vine and the olive, so in the New Testament the Church is signified by the same. Hence these words can also be understood of the Synagogue: which, especially after the coming of Christ, ceased to blossom and bear fruit, and then began to lie against Christ, to blaspheme and to deceive. For by the fig tree also, which Christ had cursed so that it withered[[Mark 11:13||]][[Mark 11:14||]][[Mark 11:20||]], the barren Synagogue was then figured.

paras.t: Abscindetur de ovili pecus. Ovile est Ecclesia : de qua pecus abscinditur, quando per negligentiam propriam vel pastoris, subditus peccat atque damnatur. Unde omni prælato præcipit Salomon in Proverbiis : Diligenter agnosce vultum pecoris tui, tuosque greges considera. Et non erit armentum in præsepibus : id est, multitudo credentium Christi pascuis non vescetur, spiritualia alimenta et Ecclesiæ sacramenta debite exquirendo; sed spiritualibus præponet temporalia atque carnalia, sicut (proh dolor !) jam videmus.
paras.en: [[3:17|the flock shall be cut off from the fold|Abscindetur de ovili pecus]]. The fold is the Church: from which the flock is cut off when, through his own negligence or the shepherd's, the subject sins and is damned. Hence Solomon in the Proverbs commands every prelate: [[Prov 27:23|Be diligent to know the countenance of thy cattle, and consider thy own flocks|Diligenter agnosce vultum pecoris tui, tuosque greges considera]] [the margin gives no reference; the words are Prov 27:23]. [[3:17|and there shall be no herd in the stalls|Et non erit armentum in præsepibus]]: that is, the multitude of believers will not feed on the pastures of Christ by duly seeking the spiritual food and the sacraments of the Church, but will set temporal and carnal things before spiritual ones, as (alas!) we now see.

paras.t: His itaque sic pereuntibus, quilibet electus dicere potest : Ego autem in Domino gaudebo, ejus bonitatem et beneficia contemplando, eumque in omnibus diligendo ac venerando. Et ponet pedes meos quasi cervorum, id est, expeditos caritatis affectus, ac fervida sancti amoris desideria mihi præstabit, quibus non solum ambulem, sed insuper curram viam mandatorum cœlestium, hostibusque salutis meæ prævaleam. Hoc convenit cuilibet idoneo pugnatori ac militi Christi, qui cum Psalmista dicere potest de Deo : Qui perfecit pedes meos tanquam cervorum.
paras.en: While these things perish in this way, any one of the elect can say: [[3:18|But I will rejoice in the Lord|Ego autem in Domino gaudebo]], by contemplating his goodness and benefits, and by loving and revering him in all things. [[3:19|and he will make my feet like the feet of harts|Et ponet pedes meos quasi cervorum]], that is, he will give me swift affections of charity and fervent desires of holy love, by which I may not only walk but even run the way of the heavenly commandments, and prevail over the enemies of my salvation. This befits every able fighter and soldier of Christ, who can say of God with the Psalmist: [[Ps 17:34|Who hath made my feet like the feet of harts|Qui perfecit pedes meos tanquam cervorum]].

paras.t: Ceterorum moralitas seu mysticus intellectus, evidens est ex præinductis. — In solo igitur Domino sit amor, fortitudo, spes et gaudium nostrum, qui est super omnia Deus sublimis et benedictus. Amen.
paras.en: The moral or mystical understanding of the rest is evident from what has been brought forward. In the Lord alone, then, be our love, our strength, our hope and our joy, who is God over all, exalted and blessed. Amen.
